title: Lists that edit like an outliner
steps: Open Lists tour. Lists are drawn with real bullets that change with depth, numbers in a right-aligned column, guides for each level, and long items that wrap under their own text. Put the cursor on a line: it shows its markdown.

On "Order seeds", press Tab: it moves under "Plan the garden"'s previous item, taking Tomatoes and Basil with it. Shift-Tab brings it back out, after its parent, and the items after it stay where they were. In Vim, >> and << do the same, and > and < on a visual selection do it to every item selected.
Alt-Down (or ]e in Vim) on "Fix the bike" moves it below "Call the plumber", its patch with it; Alt-Up (or [e) moves it back.

In the numbered list, move "Fold in the butter" up: the numbers follow. Indent "Mix the dry things": it becomes 1. under Preheat, and the rest renumber. Delete a line: the numbers close up, in the same undo step.
At the end of an item, Enter starts the next one (a todo starts a todo, a number the next number). Enter again on the empty item steps out a level, then out of the list.
Click the bullet of "Plan the garden" (or za in Vim): its children fold away behind a …; the bullet gets a ring. Click again to bring them back.
⌘⇧P, Make a numbered list on the bullets, or Make todos: the items change, their text and children stay.
Turn Lists off in the Extensions view and reload: lists are plain markdown, and Tab does nothing special.
